name: Polyglyceryl-3 distearate
description: Polyglyceryl-3 distearate (CAS 94423-19-5 ), also referenced commercially as hexaglyceryl distearate, is a polyglycerol-based emulsifier derived from glycerin and stearic acid. It stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil emulsions across personal care, food, and industrial formulations. This versatile ingredient reduces the need for synthetic ethoxylated emulsifiers in modern formulations. In skin care and cosmetics, it functions as a primary or co-emulsifier in creams, lotions, and balms, contributing to a smooth skin feel. It helps maintain a stable emulsion structure over time and across varying temperatures. Food manufacturers use it to control fat crystallization and improve texture in confectionery coatings and fat-based fillings. In color cosmetics, it aids pigment dispersion, ensuring uniform distribution in foundations and pressed powders. This ensures consistent application and color payoff for high-end cosmetic products and professional makeup lines. Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate it as a rheology modifier to adjust viscosity. It is particularly effective at improving substrate wetting in wax-based systems and specialized industrial coating applications. Polyglyceryl-3 distearate is typically supplied as a waxy solid or flake form, with a melt point suited to standard hot-process manufacturing. This physical form allows for easy handling and precise dosing during production. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent for this material. Some suppliers offer material compliant with RSPO-certified or non-GMO sourcing standards to meet specific sustainability requirements. Packaging is generally available in bags or cartons for solid material, with bulk pallet quantities standard for industrial buyers.
